name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHAPTER6_SEQ_Q01 - Sequence of steps in DNA fingerprinting

questiontext.text:
Arrange the following steps of the Southern blot hybridisation technique used in DNA fingerprinting in their correct chronological order:

  • P. Separation of DNA fragments by electrophoresis
  • Q. Digestion of DNA by restriction endonucleases
  • R. Hybridisation using labelled VNTR probe
  • S. Isolation of DNA
  • T. Transferring (blotting) of separated DNA fragments to synthetic membranes

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
DNA fingerprinting by Southern blot hybridisation requires extracting genomic DNA, cutting it into fragments, separating those fragments by size, immobilising them on a membrane, and detecting specific VNTR sequences with a radiolabelled probe.

Step 2: Step-by-Step Sequence
First, DNA is isolated from the sample cells. Second, the isolated DNA is digested using restriction endonucleases to generate fragments. Third, these DNA fragments are separated according to size by gel electrophoresis. Fourth, the separated fragments are transferred (blotted) onto synthetic membranes such as nitrocellulose or nylon. Finally, the membrane is hybridised using a labelled VNTR probe (followed by detection via autoradiography).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct chronological sequence is: Isolation of DNA \(\to\) Digestion of DNA by restriction endonucleases \(\to\) Separation of DNA fragments by electrophoresis \(\to\) Blotting onto synthetic membranes \(\to\) Hybridisation using labelled VNTR probe.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHAPTER6_SEQ_Q02 - Sequence of events during translation

questiontext.text:
Arrange the following events of protein synthesis (translation) in the correct sequence from start to finish:

  • P. Binding of ribosome to mRNA at the start codon (AUG)
  • Q. Activation of amino acids in the presence of ATP and linking to cognate tRNA
  • R. Binding of a release factor to the stop codon and release of the polypeptide
  • S. Sequential binding of charged tRNAs to mRNA codons and peptide bond formation

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Translation is the polymerisation of amino acids to form a polypeptide as directed by the base sequence of mRNA.

Step 2: Step-by-Step Sequence
In the first phase, amino acids are activated in the presence of ATP and linked to their cognate tRNAs (charging or aminoacylation of tRNA). Next, for initiation, the ribosome binds to the mRNA at the start codon (AUG), which is recognised by the initiator tRNA. During the elongation phase, charged tRNA complexes sequentially bind to complementary codons on mRNA and peptide bonds form between adjacent amino acids. Finally, a release factor binds to the stop codon, terminating translation and releasing the completed polypeptide.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct sequence is: Activation and aminoacylation of tRNA \(\to\) Binding of ribosome to mRNA at the start codon \(\to\) Sequential binding of charged tRNAs and peptide bond formation \(\to\) Binding of release factor at the stop codon and polypeptide release.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHAPTER6_SEQ_Q03 - Chronological order of landmark DNA discoveries

questiontext.text:
Arrange the following landmark discoveries in molecular biology in the correct chronological order from earliest to latest:

  • P. Hershey and Chase experiment with bacteriophages
  • Q. Identification of 'Nuclein' by Friedrich Meischer
  • R. Meselson and Stahl's experimental proof of semiconservative DNA replication
  • S. Griffith's transforming principle experiment with Streptococcus pneumoniae
  • T. Biochemical characterisation of the transforming principle by Avery, MacLeod, and McCarty

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The establishment of DNA as the genetic material and the elucidation of its replication mechanism unfolded through a series of historical experiments from the late 19th century to the mid-20th century.

Step 2: Step-by-Step Chronology
Friedrich Meischer first identified DNA as an acidic substance in the nucleus ('Nuclein') in \(1869\). Frederick Griffith demonstrated bacterial transformation in Streptococcus pneumoniae in \(1928\). Oswald Avery, Colin MacLeod, and Maclyn McCarty biochemically characterised the transforming principle as DNA between \(1933\) and \(1944\). Alfred Hershey and Martha Chase provided unequivocal proof that DNA is the genetic material in \(1952\). Finally, Matthew Meselson and Franklin Stahl proved semiconservative DNA replication in E. coli in \(1958\).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct chronological order from earliest to latest is: Identification of 'Nuclein' (\(1869\)) \(\to\) Griffith's transforming principle (\(1928\)) \(\to\) Avery, MacLeod, and McCarty's biochemical characterisation (\(1933\text{–}1944\)) \(\to\) Hershey and Chase experiment (\(1952\)) \(\to\) Meselson and Stahl experiment (\(1958\)).
